title: Against Leo's leonine teeth Luther burned the condemning bull and appealed to Charles V
pass_a_gloss: and who at last, when Pope Leo — the more unjust and with truly leonine teeth hostile to him after several most humble deprecations and protests had been made (to be read in Jena Latin Tom. I, fol. 69 at the end, and fol. 192, 210 at the end, and finally fol. 435) — sent him a message, burned the papal condemning Bull and made an appeal to Emperor Charles V (Wittenberg Latin Tom. II, fol. 44 and 45).
pass_b_english: Pope Leo answered Luther's several most humble apologies and protests (Jena Latin Tom. I, fol. 69 end; fol. 192 and 210 end; finally fol. 435) with still harsher injustice and with teeth worthy of his name.
When that leonine message came, Luther burned the condemning Bull and lodged his appeal with Emperor Charles V (Wittenberg Latin Tom. II, fol. 44–45).
source_text: etiam Papae Leoni, sibi post plures, licèt humillimas factas deprecationes & protestationes (Tomo. I. Jen. Lat. fol. 69. in fine, & fol. 192. 210. in fine, fol. denique 435. legendas,) iniquiori ac leoninis prorsùs dentibus infestanti, tandem nunciùm mittente, combustâ Papali Bullâ condemnatoriâ, factâque ad Caesarem Carolum V. provocatione, Tom. II. Wittenb. Lat. fol. 44. & 45.

choices.why: pun on Leo; keep the bite image

choices.english: sent him a message / after the papal message
choices.why: ablative absolute on Leo; Luther responds by burning the bull
